text_blocks.snippet: Common scams actively targeting Central Illinois residents include fake text messages about unpaid tolls or traffic violations, door-to-door storm repair contractors, and online shopping or package delivery smishing texts. State officials note these fraudulent alerts frequently threaten license suspension or immediate arrest.

list.snippet: Fake Toll/Traffic Texts: Fraudulent messages claiming unpaid IPASS or tollway fees, threatening driver's license suspension if you do not click a link.
Storm Chasers & Contractors: Door-to-door scammers offering quick home repairs after severe weather, demanding large cash down payments and leaving work unfinished.
Imposter Phone Calls: Scammers posing as local sheriffs or courts claiming you missed jury duty or have warrants, demanding payment via Bitcoin or gift cards.
Online Shopping & Delivery Smishing: Fake texts about delayed packages or polished fake websites offering steep discounts on popular goods.
Do not click links in unsolicited text messages regarding tolls, traffic tickets, or package deliveries.

Verify independently
by looking up official phone numbers rather than trusting caller ID or numbers provided in suspicious messages.
Never pay upfront cash or use untraceable payment methods (gift cards, wire transfers, crypto) for home repairs or government fees.

Check local resources
like the Better Business Bureau serving Central Illinois or file complaints with the Illinois Attorney General.
